new.abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (SEEG-RFTC) is used not only as a minimally invasive treatment for drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but also as an in vivo test of an SEEG-defined epileptogenic network. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 1, 2026. new.abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. new.abstract: Conductive hydrogel electrodes are vital components for achieving human-machine interfaces. new.title: A User-Function Taxonomy for Brain-Computer Interfaces: From Task Definition to Evidence.
new.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) studies are commonly compared by electrode, signal, paradigm, device, or clinical purpose. These descriptors do not identify the user-level function implemented in a task, although that function determines the appropriate endpoint. This article proposes the Type-Wield-Synthesize-Sense (TWSS) framework as a complementary taxonomy. Type involves selecting one option from alternatives specified before a decision. Wield regulates an observable state that remains correctable over time. Synthesize infers intentional expressive content without presenting alternatives at each update. new.title: Ultrasound neural interface enabling acute spinal cord monitoring and blood flow modulation.
new.abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. After wound closure, clinicians lack on-demand access to local spinal cord morphology and hemodynamics, and care therefore remains guided largely by systemic surrogates rather than direct postoperative insight into the injured cord. We present the Multimodal Ultrasound System for Injury Care (MUSIC), a temporary epidural ultrasound neural interface placed during standard decompression surgery to enable postoperative brightness-mode imaging, Doppler-derived hemodynamic monitoring, and future device-integrated ultrasound actuation. new.title: Terahertz liquid networks: a mesoscopic passive architecture for circumventing physical deadlocks in brain-computer interfaces.
new.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for major neurological disorders face physical and physiological limitations. Mechanical mismatch in rigid microelectrode arrays precipitates chronic immune rejection and irreversible central nervous system damage, whereas bandwidth scaling in traditional wireless links inevitably breaches the 1 °C tissue thermal safety threshold. To circumvent this deadlock among bandwidth, heat dissipation, and biocompatibility, this review proposes the "terahertz liquid network" architecture. Utilizing injectable plasmonic nanoparticles as free-floating relay nodes, this architecture fundamentally abolishes the mechanical shear stresses characteristic of conventional implant interfaces. new.abstract: In March 2026, China approved the world's first implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) medical device for clinical use outside clinical trials, a milestone that raises urgent questions about how legal and ethical systems should protect the brain and mind. This article examines China's emerging neurorights governance pathway, which combines the interpretive expansion of civil law personality rights, administrative ethics guidelines, and local legislative experimentation in Shenzhen. It argues that this multilayered approach is best understood as institutional experimentalism: a governance mode that uses central-level ethical soft law, subnational legislative experimentation, and existing rights frameworks to respond to technological uncertainty. new.abstract: Increasing automation and artificial intelligence (AI) integration in robot-assisted surgery may reshape surgical expertise, professional responsibility, and education. This study explored how surgical expertise might evolve over the next ten years and identified educational priorities robust across multiple plausible futures. A qualitative Technology Foresight approach combined (1) 24 semi-structured interviews with surgeons and experts in robotics, AI, augmented reality, law, and medical technology; (2) observations of 18 surgical procedures (approximately 85 h); and (3) a six-participant expert workshop. new.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support glaucoma detection and monitoring, with rapid advances in deep learning, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal prediction. new.abstract: Oral cancer presents significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges, often due to late-stage detection and tumour heterogeneity. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML), offer promising solutions by integrating multimodal biomedical data. This PRISMA-guided systematic review evaluates over 82 studies from 2015 to 2025 that apply convolutional neural networks, transformers and graph neural networks to oral cancer, using combinations of histopathology, radiology, genomics and clinical data. Previous trials confirm that elective endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an effective intervention for AAA. ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Prediabetes is a prevalent condition in which early detection and lifestyle interventions can prevent or delay progression to diabetes. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer enhanced tools for diagnosis, risk stratification, and scalable delivery of lifestyle interventions. This review synthesizes current applications of AI/ML in patients with prediabetes. ai.abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. ai.abstract: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni's action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed digital pathology by enabling biomarker prediction from high-resolution whole-slide images. However, current methods are computationally inefficient, processing thousands of redundant tiles per slide and requiring complex aggregation models. EAGLE combines task-agnostic tile selection with detailed feature extraction and is benchmarked against leading slide- and tile-level foundation models across 43 tasks from nine cancer types spanning morphology, biomarker prediction, treatment response and prognosis. ai.title: Human versus artificial intelligence: evaluating ChatGPT's performance in conducting published systematic reviews with meta-analysis in chronic pain research.
ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large-language models like Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), has demonstrated potential in streamlining research methodologies. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses, often considered the pinnacle of evidence-based medicine, are inherently time-intensive and demand meticulous planning, rigorous data extraction, thorough analysis, and careful synthesis. Despite promising applications of AI, its utility in conducting systematic reviews with meta-analysis remains unclear. This study evaluated ChatGPT's accuracy in conducting key tasks of a systematic review with meta-analysis.
